sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Kettlebell Shrug is an isolation exercise that targets the upper trapezius muscles using a pair of kettlebells held at your sides.

The offset load of kettlebells and their center of mass hanging below the hand provide a slightly different stimulus compared to dumbbells, demanding additional grip and shoulder stability.

It's a great accessory movement for building upper-back thickness, improving posture, and strengthening the traps.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Isolates and develops the upper trapezius
- Offset load increases grip and shoulder stability demand
- Neutral grip is comfortable on wrists and shoulders
- Builds upper-back thickness and posture support
- Improves grip strength and forearm endurance
- Allows unilateral focus and balance correction
- Great accessory work for deadlifts and pulls

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Trapezius (Upper), Levator Scapulae

Secondary: Rhomboids, Deltoids, Forearms and Grip, Core

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand by your sides.
2. Keep your back straight and your chest lifted.
3. Relax your arms and shoulders, palms facing your body.
4. Brace your core and look straight ahead.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Lift your shoulders as high as possible by shrugging them towards your ears.
2. Pause briefly at the top to maximize the contraction.
3. Lower your shoulders back down with control.
4. Repeat the shrug for the desired number of repetitions.
5. Focus on engaging your shoulder muscles and maintaining proper form throughout the movement.
6. Adjust the weight as needed.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Rolling the shoulders instead of lifting straight up
- Using the biceps or arms to pull the weight
- Rushing reps and missing the top contraction
- Rounding the back during the lift
- Bending the elbows during the shrug
- Not bracing the core
- Using excessive weight that limits range of motion
- Letting the head jut forward

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Pair of Kettlebells
- Non-slip Floor Surface
- Optional: Lifting Straps for heavy sets
- Optional: Chalk for improved grip
- Recommended: Flat-soled shoes for stability

sections.heading: Choosing the Right Weight
sections.content:
1. Select a load you can control through a full range of motion.
2. Prioritize feeling the trap contraction over moving heavy weight.
3. Use straps if grip fails before your traps do.
4. Progress gradually with strict form.
5. Keep reps controlled at the top and bottom.
6. Moderate to higher reps work well for trap hypertrophy.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft.
2. Grip: Neutral, palms facing your body, firm hold on the handles.
3. Torso: Upright with chest up and core braced.
4. Shoulders: Relaxed to start, retracted slightly.
5. Arms: Straight and relaxed throughout.
6. Head: Neutral, eyes looking forward.
7. Breathing: Exhale on the shrug up, inhale on the descent.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Dumbbell Shrug: Free range of motion per side
- Barbell Shrug: Heavier loading with both hands on one bar
- Trap Bar Shrug: Centered, neutral-grip variation
- Smith Machine Shrug: Fixed plane shrug variation
- Cable Shrug: Constant tension variation
- Farmers Walk Shrug: Combined carry and shrug

sections.heading: Kettlebell Shrug Variations
sections.content:
Standard Kettlebell Shrug: Both hands shrugging together
Single Arm Kettlebell Shrug: Unilateral trap focus
Paused Kettlebell Shrug: Hold at top for maximum contraction
Tempo Kettlebell Shrug: Slow eccentrics for muscle building
Rack Position Kettlebell Shrug: Kettlebells held in rack position
Seated Kettlebell Shrug: Removes lower body involvement

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Neck Pain: Reduce range and weight, keep chin tucked
Grip Issues: Use straps or chalk
Lower Back Pain: Try seated kettlebell shrugs
Shoulder Impingement: Focus on straight-up shrugs, avoid rolling
No Kettlebells: Substitute with dumbbells, barbell, or cables
Learning Stage: Start light and master the straight-up shrug pattern
